name: Undersea cables & GPS
summary: Suspected GPS jamming hit about 50 aircraft over the Netherlands, reported 16 Nov; no new undersea cable cut found
state: Dutch air traffic control LVNL said seven aircraft bound for Schiphol reported navigation problems in a GPS disruption likely caused by jamming, and a monitoring firm estimated about 50 aircraft were affected for some 20 minutes; all landed safely and the Dutch digital infrastructure authority is investigating (Innovation Origins, 16 Nov; Aviation24.be). Searches on 22 Nov found no new undersea cable cut. GNSS interference affecting aviation keeps Watch.
for_you: GPS jamming rarely affects passengers directly, as pilots use backup navigation. Ships and aircraft in the Baltic and Middle East should follow national maritime and aviation authority notices.
rubric_hit: Widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation (Netherlands, Baltic) = Watch

sources.title: Innovation Origins — GPS disruption affects dozens of aircraft over the Netherlands
Aviation24.be — Dozens of aircraft affected by suspected GPS jamming over the Netherlands

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
